messages:
sam: Pinging eng-runtime — sketch for a new synthetic traffic mode: "fuzz ramps" that mix stepped QPS ramps + microbursts to stress batching and KV warmups. Need ACKs before I add to harness.
maya: +1. what's the failure mode we're trying to reproduce? kernel selection regressions or batching badness?
sam: Both. Example: we saw kernel selector flip at 2.5k qps -> sudden 30% p99 spike. Hypothesis: batch size jumps forced slower kernel and cold KV cache thrash.
felix: Can we replay a real customer trace? Otherwise synthetic needs to match seq_len distribution and prefix locality.
sam: plan: 1) generate base Poisson steady qps 2) every N mins inject short spikes (50-200ms at 5-10x) 3) long-tail slow dribble to shape p99 4) randomized seed for kernel path diversity
jia: How do we model KV cache behavior? warmup vs eviction?
sam: We'll include sticky keys (80% of requests hit small hot keyset), and occasional full-sweep fanouts to flush LRU. Also TTL-based jitter on key lifetimes.
maya: Need metrics capture: per-kernel invocation counts, batch-size histogram, kv_hit_rate (prefix vs token-level), scheduler queue length.
sam: Also perf counters: kernel_time_ms, per-request latency broken by stage (enqueue, batch_wait, exec, kv_fetch).
ci-bot: deploy-test: new traffic mode 'fuzz-ramp-v1' added to repo branch perf/fuzz-ramp
felix: Run apples-to-apples: same seed, same model weights, same hw. Use pinned kernel versions and record config.json alongside runs.
sam: Let's add a small command snippet devs can run locally:
```bash
./traffic-gen --mode fuzz-ramp --seed 42 --qps-base 300 --spike-mult 8 --spike-dur 120 --hotset 500
```
maya: Could we add a "kernel-drain" toggle to simulate slow kernel selection recompile? i.e., stall chosen kernel for X ms to measure fallback.
sam: good idea. Also add a KV warm-start flag to pre-populate 95% hot keys.
jia: I ran a short test on stage: p95 stayed stable but p99 jumped to 1.9s during spike. Attaching sample output:
```
[2027-06-12T13:04:33Z] qps=2400 spike=8x batch_mean=20 batch_p95=64 kernel=fast_conv run_time=120s p99=1890ms kv_hit=0.78
```
sam: That p99 looks like batch packing induced stragglers. Let's profile a trace with /debug/batches endpoint.
felix: Found 2 hotspots: memcpy on quantized path and lock contention in batch dispatcher when batch size >48.
maya: Could be scheduler spinning when KV fetch pending. Add backpressure threshold on batch buffer and adaptive batch timeout.
sam: Added heuristic: if avg_kv_latency > 15ms, reduce target_batch_size by 30% and set batch_timeout=8ms.
ops-bot: alert: perf/regression detected on perf-suite/fuzz-ramp-v1 compare to baseline: p99 +22% kernel_switches +180%
sam: Oof. Need root cause; maybe kernel auto-selector weights tuned for steady loads and misclassify under bursts.
jia: For apples-to-apples we should save profiler traces, kernel selection logs, and exact traffic seed in s3://redwood-perf/fuzz-ramp/1812349876/
sam: agree. I'll increment run id and kick off full 1hr sweep with different seeds and collect metrics.
maya: One more ask: make generator output compact event log for replay harness. Format: one line per request with seq_len, key_id, timestamp_offset_ms, rand_flags.
sam: ok will add --replay-log option.
felix: Quick question: does the generator emulate token-at-a-time arrival (streaming) vs full-input? Need both.
sam: yes flag --streaming with per-token delta distribution.
jia: I'll try the staging run with --streaming and post results.
sam: thanks all. If no objections I'll merge perf/fuzz-ramp by EOD. :thumbsup: 
maya: no objections. +1
felix: go for it.
ci-bot: pipeline passed for perf/fuzz-ramp branch (tests: unit, perf-smoke). Build id: 5467
